generics.name: Furosemide
generics.mechanismOfAction: Furosemide reversibly inhibits the luminal Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter (NKCC2) in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle. This blocks reabsorption of sodium, potassium, and chloride, abolishing the medullary concentration gradient and causing high-volume isotonic diuresis. It also induces renal prostaglandin-mediated capacitance venodilation.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Luminal Na+/K+/2Cl- cotransporter 2 (NKCC2) in thick ascending limb of loop of Henle

indications.name: Congestive Heart Failure (Acute pulmonary edema & chronic volume overload)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: First-line symptomatic relief of fluid congestion (DGHS & ESC Guidelines)

indications.name: Hepatic Cirrhosis with Ascites and Peripheral Edema
Nephrotic Syndrome and CKD Fluid Retention
Hypertensive Crisis with Fluid Overload

contraindications.reason: Risk of cumulative ototoxicity and metabolic encephalopathy
Precipitates fatal cardiac arrhythmias
Hypokalemia increases renal ammonia production

dosageGuidance.adult: Oral: 20-40 mg initial once daily; titrate up to 80-160 mg/day. IV: 40 mg slow IV bolus over 2 min in acute pulmonary edema.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: Oral: 1-2 mg/kg once daily (Max 6 mg/kg/day). IV: 1 mg/kg slow IV.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Start at lowest adult dose (20 mg) to prevent severe orthostatic hypotension.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take in the morning to prevent nocturia.

doseAdjustment.renal: Higher doses (80-250 mg IV) needed in eGFR < 30 mL/min; maximum IV rate 4 mg/min to prevent ototoxicity.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Careful titration in cirrhosis to avoid rapid intravascular depletion.

seriousWarnings: Black Box: Profound fluid and electrolyte depletion, acute hypovolemic shock, cardiac arrest from hypokalemia, and ototoxicity if infused > 4 mg/min.

precautions: Monitor serum K+, Na+, and creatinine regularly. Advise dietary potassium (bananas, green coconut water).

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Baseline, day 3-5 IV, then every 1-3 months

generics.foodInteractions: Oral absorption delayed by high-fat meals. Take on empty stomach with water.

pregnancyInfo.details: Crosses placenta. Decreases placental perfusion. Indicated only for maternal pulmonary edema.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in small amounts. High doses may inhibit lactation.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: May cause nephrocalcinosis in premature neonates.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: High risk of orthostatic hypotension and falls.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Profound hypovolemia, hypotension, hypokalemic arrhythmias.
overdoseInformation.management: IV normal saline and KCl under ECG monitoring. No specific antidote.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 30°C in a dry place protected from light.

bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: অতিরিক্ত প্রস্রাবের কারণে লবণ ও পানির মারাত্মক ঘাটতি হতে পারে; মাংসপেশিতে টান লাগলে ডাক্তার দেখান।

pharmacologyLearning.pathwaySummary: Loop of Henle NKCC2 inhibition -> loss of medullary gradient -> solute diuresis + venous capacitance dilation.
pharmacologyLearning.receptorTarget: NKCC2 cotransporter in thick ascending limb

vivaQuestions.question: Why is Furosemide high-ceiling?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: ফিউরোসেমাইডকে কেন হাই-সিলিং ডাইইউরেটিক বলে?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Steep dose-response curve excreting up to 25% of filtered sodium load.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Thick ascending limb reabsorbs 25% of filtered sodium.

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Furosemide provide relief before diuresis starts?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: প্রস্রাব শুরুর আগেই ফিউরোসেমাইড কেন দ্রুত আরাম দেয়?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Within 5-15 min of IV injection, it stimulates renal prostaglandin release, inducing systemic venodilation and reducing cardiac preload.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: NSAIDs blunt this early venodilatory action.

recallFlashcards.front: Molecular target of Furosemide?
recallFlashcards.back: NKCC2 symporter in thick ascending limb of loop of Henle.

recallFlashcards.front: Maximum recommended IV injection rate?
recallFlashcards.back: 4 mg/minute to avoid ototoxicity.

practiceSba.question: Initial hemodynamic relief in acute pulmonary edema from IV furosemide is due to?
practiceSba.explanation: Venodilation occurs within 5-15 min before diuresis starts.

clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 68M with bilateral pedal edema and orthopnea.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Treated with IV furosemide, developed severe hypokalemic cramps.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: Immediate action?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Pause furosemide, infuse IV potassium chloride with cardiac telemetry.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: Oral bioavailability is 50% to 70% (delayed and reduced by food). IV administration is 100% bioavailable.
pharmacokinetics.onsetOfAction: Oral: 30 to 60 minutes (peak 1 to 2 hours, duration 6 to 8 hours). IV: Within 5 minutes (peak 30 minutes, duration 2 hours).
pharmacokinetics.halfLife: Terminal half-life is 0.5 to 2 hours (prolonged up to 9 hours in end-stage renal disease or hepatic cirrhosis).
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Minimal hepatic metabolism (~10-15%); predominantly glucuronidation in the kidney and liver.
pharmacokinetics.excretion: Approximately 60% to 80% excreted unchanged in urine via active renal proximal tubular secretion (OAT1/OAT3); remainder excreted in feces.
pharmacokinetics.proteinBinding: 91% to 99%, primarily bound to serum albumin.

generics.name: Hydrochlorothiazide
generics.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits the Na+/Cl- cotransporter (NCCT) in the luminal membrane of the early distal convoluted tubule. This increases urinary excretion of sodium, chloride, and water (~5% of filtered load). Unlike loop diuretics, thiazides reduce urinary calcium excretion by enhancing basolateral Na+/Ca2+ exchange, producing hypocalciuria and protecting against osteoporotic bone loss.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Luminal Na+/Cl- cotransporter (NCC / SLC12A3) in early distal convoluted tubule

indications.name: Essential Hypertension
indications.guidelineRecommendation: First-line monotherapy or combination with ARB/ACEI (NHF Guidelines)

indications.name: Recurrent Idiopathic Calcium Nephrolithiasis

contraindications.reason: Ineffective when eGFR < 30 mL/min; loop diuretics required instead
Risk of fatal cardiac arrhythmias and cerebral edema
Competes with uric acid secretion in proximal tubule

dosageGuidance.adult: Hypertension: 12.5 mg to 25 mg once daily in the morning (doses > 25 mg increase metabolic adverse effects without greater BP reduction).
dosageGuidance.paediatric: 1-2 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Initial 12.5 mg daily; monitor for hyponatremia.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take with breakfast in the morning.

doseAdjustment.renal: Ineffective in eGFR < 30 mL/min; switch to loop diuretic.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Caution in severe hepatic disease to prevent encephalopathy.

seriousWarnings: Severe Thiazide-Induced Hyponatremia: Elderly female patients are at high risk of rapid, severe hyponatremia leading to seizures and cerebral edema.

precautions: Monitor serum sodium, potassium, and uric acid regularly. Caution in diabetes.
generics.foodInteractions: Can be taken with or without food.

pregnancyInfo.details: Crosses placenta. Not recommended for gestational hypertension due to maternal hypovolemia.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in breast milk; high doses can suppress lactation.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Safe in children for hypertension and edema.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: High incidence of hyponatremia and hypokalemia. Doses above 25 mg should be avoided.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Severe dehydration, lethargy, hyponatremic encephalopathy.
overdoseInformation.management: Electrolyte repletion with normal saline; monitor vital signs.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C in airtight container.

bilingualNotes.classBn: থায়াজাইড ডাইইউরেটিক (ডিস্টাল টিউবিউলে কাজ করা রক্তচাপ কমানোর ওষুধ)
bilingualNotes.mechanismSummaryBn: কিডনির ডিস্টাল পেঁচানো নালিকায় সোডিয়াম পুনঃশোষণ বন্ধ করে রক্তচাপ কমায় এবং প্রস্রাবে ক্যালসিয়াম বের হওয়া রোধ করে।
bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: সকালে সেবন করুন। নিয়মিত রক্তে সোডিয়াম ও পটাশিয়াম পরীক্ষা করান। বাতের ব্যথা থাকলে ডাক্তারকে জানান।
bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: বয়স্ক রোগীদের ক্ষেত্রে হঠাৎ রক্তে সোডিয়াম কমে গিয়ে মারাত্মক অচেতনতা দেখা দিতে পারে।

pharmacologyLearning.pathwaySummary: Early DCT Na+/Cl- cotransporter (NCC) blockade -> ~5% natriuresis + enhanced basolateral Na+/Ca2+ exchange (hypocalciuria).

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Hydrochlorothiazide cause hypocalciuria while Furosemide causes hypercalciuria?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: থায়াজাইড কেন ক্যালসিয়াম ক্ষয় কমায় কিন্তু লুপ ডাইইউরেটিক ক্যালসিয়াম ক্ষয় বাড়ায়?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Thiazides block NCC in the DCT, lowering intracellular Na+ and stimulating basolateral Na+/Ca2+ antiporter to reabsorb calcium. Furosemide abolishes lumen-positive transepithelial potential in loop of Henle, eliminating driving force for paracellular Ca2+ and Mg2+ reabsorption.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Thiazides protect bones in osteoporosis and prevent recurrent calcium renal stones.

recallFlashcards.front: Site of action of Hydrochlorothiazide?
recallFlashcards.back: Early distal convoluted tubule (blocks NCC cotransporter).

recallFlashcards.front: Effect of Thiazides on urinary calcium?
recallFlashcards.back: Decreases urinary calcium excretion (causes hypocalciuria / hypercalcemia).

practiceSba.question: A 64-year-old female with osteoporosis and hypertension needs a diuretic that helps preserve bone density. Which drug is preferred?
practiceSba.explanation: Hydrochlorothiazide reduces urinary calcium excretion, increasing bone mineral density.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Hypertension & Recurrent Calcium Stones
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 48M with recurrent calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis and BP 152/94 mmHg.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Started on Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily. 24h urinary calcium dropped by 50% and BP normalized.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: Why is HCTZ preferred over Furosemide in this case?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Furosemide would worsen hypercalciuria and promote stone formation, whereas HCTZ prevents calcium precipitation in renal tubules.

generics.name: Spironolactone
generics.mechanismOfAction: Competitive antagonist of the cytosolic mineralocorticoid (aldosterone) receptor in principal and intercalated cells of the late distal tubule and cortical collecting duct. It prevents aldosterone-induced synthesis of epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) and basolateral Na+/K+-ATPase pumps. This blunts sodium reabsorption while halting potassium and hydrogen ion excretion. In heart failure, it blocks myocardial and vascular fibrosis driven by pathological aldosterone excess.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Intracellular Mineralocorticoid Receptor (MR) in renal collecting tubule and myocardium

indications.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF, NYHA Class II-IV)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: Proven 30% mortality reduction in RALES clinical trial

indications.name: Cirrhotic Ascites and Secondary Hyperaldosteronism
indications.note: Drug of choice for ascites (100 mg daily titrated up to 400 mg)

indications.name: Resistant Hypertension (Fourth-line add-on agent)

contraindications.reason: High risk of fatal cardiac arrest from peaked T waves and ventricular arrhythmia

contraindications.condition: Acute renal failure / severe CKD (eGFR < 30 mL/min)
contraindications.reason: Inability to excrete potassium leads to rapid toxic hyperkalemia

dosageGuidance.adult: Heart Failure: 12.5 mg to 25 mg once daily (Max 50 mg/day). Cirrhotic Ascites: 100 mg initial once daily, titrated up to 400 mg/day. Resistant Hypertension: 25-50 mg daily.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: 1-3 mg/kg/day in 1-2 divided doses.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Initial 12.5-25 mg daily with strict K+ monitoring.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take with meals to enhance absorption and reduce GI irritation.

doseAdjustment.renal: eGFR 30-50 mL/min: start 12.5 mg every other day; eGFR < 30 mL/min: contraindicated.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Metabolized into active canrenone; monitor electrolytes closely in cirrhosis.

seriousWarnings: Black Box: Severe Life-Threatening Hyperkalemia. Concomitant use with ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or potassium supplements without strict monitoring can precipitate fatal cardiac arrhythmias.

precautions: Never combine with potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium. Avoid in acute renal failure.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Baseline, 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 3 months

generics.foodInteractions: Food increases oral bioavailability by ~90-100%. Always take with meals.

pregnancyInfo.details: Antiandrogenic properties can cause feminization of male fetuses. Avoid in pregnancy.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in breast milk in negligible amounts; compatible per AAP.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Used for pediatric ascites and heart failure under specialist supervision.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: High risk of hyperkalemia. Avoid doses above 25 mg/day in heart failure.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Severe hyperkalemia, somnolence, confusion, dehydration, flaccid paralysis.
overdoseInformation.management: IV Calcium gluconate 10% for cardiac membrane stabilization, IV insulin + 25% dextrose, salbutamol nebulization, and urgent hemodialysis.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

bilingualNotes.mechanismSummaryBn: কিডনির কালেক্টিং ডাক্টে অ্যালডোস্টেরন হরমোনকে ব্লক করে প্রস্রাবের সাথে পটাশিয়াম ক্ষয় হওয়া বন্ধ করে এবং অতিরিক্ত লবণ ও পানি বের করে দেয়।
bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: খাবারের সাথে সেবন করুন। রক্তে পটাশিয়াম বেড়ে যাওয়ার মারাত্মক ঝুঁকি থাকায় চিকিৎসকের অনুমতি ছাড়া ডাবের পানি বা পটাশিয়াম সাপ্লিমেন্ট গ্রহণ করবেন না। পুরুষদের ক্ষেত্রে স্তন বৃদ্ধি (গাইনোকোমাস্টিয়া) হতে পারে।
bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: রক্তে পটাশিয়াম মাত্রাতিরিক্ত বৃদ্ধি পেলে বুক ধড়ফড় ও হার্ট অ্যাটাক হতে পারে; অনিয়মিত হৃদস্পন্দন বা দুর্বলতা অনুভব করলে তাৎক্ষণিক হাসপাতালে যোগাযোগ করুন।

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Spironolactone cause painful gynecomastia in males, and which alternative drug avoids this?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: স্পাইরোনোল্যাকটোন কেন পুরুষদের স্তন বৃদ্ধি ঘটায় এবং এর বিকল্প কী?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Spironolactone is a non-selective steroid that cross-reacts with androgen receptors (antagonist) and progesterone receptors (agonist). Eplerenone is a selective mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist with 1000-fold lower affinity for androgen receptors, avoiding gynecomastia.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Eplerenone has higher MR selectivity and zero gynecomastia risk.

recallFlashcards.front: Active metabolite of Spironolactone?
recallFlashcards.back: Canrenone (responsible for prolonged half-life of 16-20 hours).

recallFlashcards.front: Major endocrine side effect in males?
recallFlashcards.back: Gynecomastia and testicular atrophy due to antiandrogenic effect.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Cirrhotic Ascites & Electrolyte Balancing
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 52M with hepatitis B cirrhosis and gross abdominal ascites.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Started on Furosemide 40 mg + Spironolactone 100 mg daily. Ascites gradually resolved without hypokalemia.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: Why are these two diuretics combined in cirrhosis?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Furosemide causes hypokalemia, whereas spironolactone retains potassium and blocks secondary hyperaldosteronism. Combining them in a 100:40 ratio produces neutral potassium balance and optimal natriuresis.

generics.name: Enalapril
generics.mechanismOfAction: Enalapril is an ethyl ester prodrug rapidly bioactivated by hepatic esterases into enalaprilat, a potent competitive inhibitor of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE / peptidyl dipeptidase). ACE inhibition halts the conversion of angiotensin I into angiotensin II. This results in decreased systemic vascular resistance, decreased aldosterone-mediated sodium retention, and attenuation of ventricular remodeling, while elevating bradykinin levels.

indications.guidelineRecommendation: First-line agent in diabetes, CKD, or left ventricular dysfunction (NHF Guidelines)

indications.name: Heart Failure with Reduced Ejection Fraction (HFrEF)

bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: প্রথম ডোজটি রাতে শোবার সময় সেবন করুন। শুষ্ক কাশি দেখা দিলে চিকিৎসককে জানান। পটাশিয়াম যুক্ত লবণ এড়িয়ে চলুন।

vivaQuestions.question: What is the molecular mediator of ACEI-induced dry cough?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: এসিই ইনহিবিটর জনিত কাশির কারণ কী?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Bradykinin and substance P accumulation due to inhibition of kininase II (identical to ACE).
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Switching to an ARB eliminates the cough because ARBs block AT1 receptors without inhibiting kininase II.

recallFlashcards.front: Active metabolite of Enalapril?
recallFlashcards.back: Enalaprilat.

practiceSba.question: A diabetic hypertensive male on enalapril develops dry cough. Most appropriate switch?
practiceSba.explanation: Switching to an ARB (Losartan) preserves blood pressure control without causing cough.

generics.name: Losartan
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Angiotensin II Receptor Blocker (Selective AT1 Antagonist)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Losartan potassium selectively competitively blocks the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor. This prevents all downstream actions of angiotensin II, including vasoconstriction, aldosterone release, and cardiac remodeling, without inhibiting kininase II or elevating bradykinin. Its active metabolite E-3174 provides long-lasting insurmountable AT1 blockade. Losartan also uniquely inhibits renal URAT1, producing modest uricosuria.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Angiotensin II Type 1 (AT1) Receptor & Renal URAT1

indications.name: Hypertension (Especially in patients intolerant to ACE inhibitors due to cough)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: First-line therapy in NHF and international guidelines

indications.name: Diabetic Nephropathy in Type 2 Diabetes with Proteinuria

generics.name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Aspirin covalently and irreversibly acetylates a serine residue (Ser529 in COX-1, Ser516 in COX-2) near the catalytic active site of cyclooxygenase. In platelets, which lack protein synthesis machinery, this permanently blocks thromboxane A2 (TXA2) production for the entire lifespan of the platelet (7-10 days), providing potent lifelong antiplatelet aggregation. Higher doses inhibit endothelial prostacyclin (PGI2) synthesis and peripheral COX enzymes, mediating anti-inflammatory and analgesic effects.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is aspirin unique among NSAIDs in its antiplatelet effect?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: অন্যান্য এনএসএআইডি এর তুলনায় অ্যাসপিরিনের অ্যান্টিপ্লাটলেট প্রভাব অনন্য কেন?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Aspirin irreversibly inhibits COX-1 by covalent acetylation of Ser529. Because mature platelets lack nuclei and ribosomes, they cannot synthesize new COX-1 enzymes; inhibition lasts for the entire platelet lifespan (7-10 days).

vivaQuestions.question: What is Reye Syndrome and why is aspirin contraindicated in febrile children?

generics.name: Clopidogrel
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Thienopyridine Antiplatelet Agent (Irreversible P2Y12 ADP Receptor Antagonist)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Clopidogrel is an inactive thienopyridine prodrug that requires two-step hepatic bioactivation by cytochrome P450 enzymes (predominantly CYP2C19, CYP3A4, CYP1A2, and CYP2B6) to generate its active thiol metabolite. The active metabolite irreversibly binds via disulfide bonding to the platelet purinergic P2Y12 adenosine diphosphate (ADP) receptor. This prevents ADP-mediated activation of the glycoprotein IIb/IIIa (GPIIb/IIIa) complex, irreversibly blocking fibrinogen cross-linking and platelet aggregation for the lifespan of the platelet.

Omeprazole is a strong competitive inhibitor of CYP2C19, substantially reducing plasma levels of clopidogrel active thiol metabolite and increasing recurrent coronary stent thrombosis. The clinical solution is to switch the PPI to Pantoprazole, which is metabolized via sulfoconjugation and does not inhibit CYP2C19.

generics.name: Warfarin
generics.mechanismOfAction: Inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase complex 1 (VKORC1), blocking the regeneration of reduced vitamin K (vitamin KH2). Reduced vitamin K is an essential cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which carboxylates glutamic acid residues on coagulation factors II (prothrombin), VII, IX, and X, as well as endogenous anticoagulant proteins C and S. Incomplete carboxylation renders these clotting factors biologically inactive. Because pre-existing circulating factors must be degraded, full clinical antithrombotic effect takes 3 to 5 days (governed by the half-life of prothrombin: ~60-72 hours).

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Warfarin paradoxically cause skin necrosis in the first 24 to 48 hours of initiation?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: শুরু করার প্রথম ১-২ দিনে ওয়ারফারিন কেন উল্টো রক্তনালী জমাট বাঁধিয়ে স্কিন নেক্রোসিস করতে পারে?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Endogenous anticoagulant Protein C has a very short half-life (~6 to 8 hours), much shorter than procoagulant factors II, IX, and X. Warfarin depletes Protein C first, precipitating a transient, paradoxically prothrombotic state leading to microvascular cutaneous thrombosis and skin necrosis, especially in patients with pre-existing protein C deficiency. This is why heparin bridging is mandatory.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Always bridge with Heparin/LMWH until INR is within therapeutic range for 2 consecutive days.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the immediate reversal agent for life-threatening bleeding on Warfarin?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: ওয়ারফারিনের কারণে মারাত্মক রক্তক্ষরণে সবচেয়ে দ্রুত কার্যকরী অ্যান্টিডোট কোনটি?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: 4-Factor Prothrombin Complex Concentrate (PCC) along with slow IV Vitamin K1. PCC provides pre-formed active clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X) within 15 minutes, while Vitamin K takes 6 to 24 hours to stimulate new hepatic synthesis.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: PCC is superior to FFP because of rapid reconstitution, small infusion volume, and absence of fluid overload risk.

generics.name: Heparin (Unfractionated Heparin)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Unfractionated heparin binds via a specific high-affinity pentasaccharide sequence to antithrombin III (ATIII), inducing a conformational change that accelerates antithrombin’s catalytic inactivation of thrombin (factor IIa), factor Xa, and factors IXa, XIa, and XIIa by over 1,000-fold. To inactivate thrombin (IIa), heparin must form a ternary molecular bridge wrapping around both antithrombin and thrombin (requiring at least 18 saccharide units). For factor Xa inhibition, only the pentasaccharide binding to antithrombin is necessary.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the structural difference in how Heparin and LMWH inactivate Thrombin vs Factor Xa?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: থ্রম্বিন ও ফ্যাক্টর ১০এ নিষ্ক্রিয়করণে হেপারিন ও লো-মলিকুলার-ওয়েট হেপারিনের মধ্যে পার্থক্যের কারণ কী?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Inactivation of thrombin (IIa) requires a long polysaccharide chain (>= 18 saccharide units) that can bridge and wrap around both ATIII and thrombin simultaneously. Inactivation of factor Xa requires only the pentasaccharide sequence binding to ATIII without bridging. Unfractionated heparin has equal 1:1 activity against IIa and Xa. LMWH molecules are shorter (< 18 units), so they effectively inactivate Xa but have much less activity against IIa (Xa:IIa ratio 3:1 to 4:1).

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 60F receiving IV heparin for 7 days post-hip surgery.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Platelet count plunges from 250,000 to 45,000/μL. She suddenly develops acute left leg swelling and cyanosis due to new DVT.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What catastrophic immune reaction is this?

These complexes cross-link FcγRIIa receptors on platelets, causing massive platelet activation and widespread thrombosis. Heparin must be halted immediately and replaced with a non-heparin anticoagulant (Argatroban).

generics.name: Amoxicillin
generics.mechanismOfAction: Bactericidal beta-lactam antibiotic that competitively inhibits bacterial transpeptidase enzymes (penicillin-binding proteins, PBPs, chiefly PBP-1A and PBP-2). This prevents the cross-linking of linear peptidoglycan strands in the bacterial cell wall during active bacterial cell division. The resulting weakened cell wall cannot withstand osmotic pressure, leading to bacterial cell lysis mediated by bacterial autolysins and murein hydrolases. Amoxicillin has superior oral bioavailability (75-90%) compared to ampicillin and absorption is unaffected by food.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is amoxicillin better absorbed orally than ampicillin?

vivaQuestions.question: Why is amoxicillin combined with clavulanic acid?

generics.name: Azithromycin
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Azalide / Macrolide Antibiotic (50S Ribosomal Subunit Inhibitor)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Azithromycin is a semi-synthetic azalide antibiotic derived by inserting a nitrogen atom into the 14-membered lactone ring of erythromycin, forming a 15-membered ring. It reversibly binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit (specifically the 23S rRNA) of susceptible microorganisms. This halts transpeptidation and translocation of nascent peptidyl-tRNA, inhibiting RNA-dependent bacterial protein synthesis. It concentrates intensely within intracellular lysosomal compartments of phagocytes, macrophages, and neutrophils, which actively transport the drug to sites of infection (producing tissue concentrations up to 50 times higher than plasma levels). It has a prolonged terminal half-life of 68 hours, enabling once-daily dosing and short 3- to 5-day treatment courses.

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Azithromycin only require a 3 to 5 day course?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: অ্যাজিথ্রোমাইসিনের কোর্স মাত্র ৩ থেকে ৫ দিন কেন?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Azithromycin has extensive tissue sequestration within phagocytes and fibroblasts, providing tissue half-life of 68 hours and maintaining therapeutic tissue levels for 7-10 days after completion.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Tissue concentrations are 10-50 times higher than plasma concentrations.

recallFlashcards.front: Target of Azithromycin?
recallFlashcards.back: 50S ribosomal subunit (23S rRNA).

recallFlashcards.front: Major cardiovascular risk?
recallFlashcards.back: QTc prolongation and Torsades de Pointes.

practiceSba.question: Which antibiotic is first-line oral therapy for uncomplicated genital Chlamydia trachomatis infection as a single 1 g dose?
practiceSba.explanation: A single 1 g oral dose of Azithromycin achieves cure rates > 95% in urogenital chlamydial infections.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Atypical Pneumonia with Prolonged QTc
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 72-year-old male with COPD and dry persistent cough, taking amiodarone.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Prescribed azithromycin for atypical pneumonia; baseline ECG shows QTc of 490 ms. On day 2, QTc prolongs to 530 ms.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What immediate clinical management is mandated?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Discontinue azithromycin immediately due to additive risk of fatal Torsades de Pointes ventricular arrhythmia. Switch to an alternative non-QT-prolonging antibiotic (e.g., doxycycline) and check serum potassium and magnesium.

generics.name: Ceftriaxone
generics.mechanismOfAction: Third-generation cephalosporin with excellent bactericidal activity against Gram-negative bacilli, Neisseria, and Streptococcus. It binds to and acetylates bacterial penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs), inhibiting the final transpeptidation step of cell wall synthesis. It is highly stable against common plasmid-mediated bacterial beta-lactamases. Notably, ceftriaxone exhibits high penetrance across the inflamed blood-brain barrier (achieving therapeutic CSF levels) and has a prolonged elimination half-life of 8 hours, allowing convenient once-daily or twice-daily dosing.

indications.name: Bacterial Meningitis (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, H. influenzae)

Severe Hospital Sepsis, Intra-abdominal Infections, and Pyelonephritis
Uncomplicated Anogenital Gonorrhea (Neisseria gonorrhoeae)
Surgical Antimicrobial Prophylaxis

common: Local phlebitis / pain at injection site
uncommon: Biliary sludge / pseudolithiasis (reversible ceftriaxone-calcium precipitation in gallbladder)
seriousWarnings: Fatal Neonatal Calcium-Ceftriaxone Precipitation: Never co-administer ceftriaxone with calcium-containing IV solutions (Ringer’s Lactate, Hartmann’s solution) in neonates.

precautions: Always verify allergy history. Reversible biliary colic/sludge can occur on high-dose therapy (> 2 g/day for > 14 days).

monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Immediate cessation and resuscitation if wheezing or hypotension develops

generics.foodInteractions: Administered parenterally (IV/IM); food not applicable.

pregnancyInfo.details: Crosses placenta; extensive clinical experience indicates safety in pregnancy.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in small amounts in breast milk; compatible with breastfeeding (AAP / WHO).

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates and premature infants due to kernicterus risk.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Safe in elderly; dual excretion prevents excessive accumulation.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Neuromuscular excitability, myoclonus, encephalopathy, seizures.
overdoseInformation.management: Symptomatic supportive treatment, anticonvulsants (diazepam). Not dialyzable.

generics.storageInformation: Store powder below 25°C protected from light. Reconstituted solutions are stable for 24 hours at room temperature (25°C) and 3 days at 2-8°C.

bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: নবজাতকদের ক্ষেত্রে ক্যালসিয়ামযুক্ত স্যালাইনের (রিঙ্গার ল্যাকটেট) সাথে কখনোই একসাথে প্রয়োগ করা যাবে না।

vivaQuestions.question: Why is Ceftriaxone given once daily unlike Ampicillin or Cefotaxime?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: অন্যান্য অ্যান্টিবায়োটিকের বিপরীতে সেফট্রিয়াক্সন দিনে একবার কেন দেওয়া যায়?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Ceftriaxone has high plasma protein binding (~90-95%) and a long elimination half-life of 8 hours, maintaining bactericidal concentrations above MIC for 24 hours.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Elimination is dual: 60% renal and 40% biliary.

recallFlashcards.front: Why contraindicated with IV calcium in neonates?
recallFlashcards.back: Fatal insoluble ceftriaxone-calcium salt precipitation in lungs and kidneys.

practiceSba.question: Empirical intravenous antibiotic of choice for acute community-acquired bacterial meningitis in an adult is?
practiceSba.explanation: High-dose Ceftriaxone penetrates inflamed meninges and provides bactericidal activity against pneumococcus and meningococcus.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Pseudolithiasis / Biliary Sludge on High-Dose Therapy
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 24-year-old female treated with IV Ceftriaxone 2 g daily for 14 days for severe typhoid fever.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Develops right upper quadrant pain. Ultrasound shows reversible gallbladder shadows (pseudolithiasis).
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What is the etiology and management?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Ceftriaxone-calcium salt precipitates in bile during high-dose prolonged therapy. It is reversible and typically resolves spontaneously upon discontinuation.

generics.name: Ciprofloxacin
generics.mechanismOfAction: Potent bactericidal fluoroquinolone that inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) in Gram-negative bacteria and topoisomerase IV in Gram-positive bacteria. DNA gyrase is essential for negative supercoiling and relaxing topological strain during DNA replication and transcription; topoisomerase IV separates daughter DNA molecules during cell division. Inhibition produces double-stranded DNA breaks and rapid cell death.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Bacterial DNA Gyrase (GyrA subunit) & Topoisomerase IV (ParC subunit)

indications.name: Complicated Urinary Tract Infections and Acute Pyelonephritis
Severe Bacterial Diarrhea / Bacillary Dysentery (Shigella, Campylobacter, E. coli)
Bone and Joint Infections (Chronic Osteomyelitis due to Gram-negative bacilli)
Post-Exposure Prophylaxis and Treatment of Inhalation Anthrax (Bacillus anthracis)

contraindications.condition: Known hypersensitivity to ciprofloxacin or fluoroquinolones
contraindications.reason: Risk of anaphylaxis and severe cutaneous adverse reactions
Severe hypotension and sedation due to potent CYP1A2 inhibition

contraindications.condition: History of fluoroquinolone-induced tendinitis or tendon rupture
contraindications.reason: High recurrence of Achilles tendon rupture

dosageGuidance.adult: Oral: 250 mg to 750 mg every 12 hours. IV: 200 mg to 400 mg every 12 hours infused slowly over 60 minutes.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: 10 to 20 mg/kg/dose every 12 hours (restricted to complicated UTI, pyelonephritis, or inhalation anthrax).
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Adult dosing guided by renal function.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take with full glass of water. Maintain high fluid intake to prevent crystalluria.

doseAdjustment.renal: eGFR 30-50 mL/min: 250-500 mg every 12h; eGFR < 30 mL/min: 250-500 mg every 18-24 hours.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: No dose adjustment required.

seriousWarnings: Black Box Warning: Disabling and Potentially Irreversible Serious Adverse Reactions (Tendinitis and Tendon Rupture, Peripheral Neuropathy, and CNS Toxicities). Reserve for use in patients who have no alternative treatment options. Avoid in patients with aortic aneurysm.

precautions: Instruct patients to immediately stop ciprofloxacin at the first sign of tendon pain or inflammation. Avoid direct sunlight / UV exposure due to photosensitivity. Avoid multivalent cation supplements (Iron, Calcium, Antacids) within 2 hours.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: In cardiac patients or when combined with other QT-prolonging drugs

generics.foodInteractions: Dairy products (milk, yogurt) and calcium-fortified juices severely reduce oral absorption (chelation with multivalent cations). Take 2 hours before or 4 hours after dairy or calcium/iron supplements.

pregnancyInfo.details: Causes arthropathy and cartilage erosion in weight-bearing juvenile joints in animal studies; avoid in pregnancy unless no alternative.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in human milk; potential risk of joint damage. Alternative antibiotics preferred.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Generally avoided in children due to cartilage toxicity, but approved for complicated UTI and anthrax when benefits outweigh risks.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Elderly patients over 60 taking corticosteroids have the highest risk of tendon rupture. Start with lower doses.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness, confusion, tremors, seizures, acute renal failure from crystalluria.
overdoseInformation.management: Gastric lavage, activated charcoal, maintain high hydration to prevent crystalluria. Hemodialysis removes only 10%.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C in a dry place protected from light.

vivaQuestions.question: Why are fluoroquinolones contraindicated in children and pregnancy?

vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Fluoroquinolones cause arthropathy and articular cartilage erosion in juvenile weight-bearing joints in animal studies, and pose tendon rupture risks.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Black box warning for Achilles tendonitis and tendon rupture.

recallFlashcards.front: Major black box warning for Fluoroquinolones?
recallFlashcards.back: Tendonitis and tendon rupture (especially Achilles tendon), and peripheral neuropathy.

practiceSba.question: Ciprofloxacin absorption is severely diminished if ingested concurrently with which of the following?
practiceSba.explanation: Polyvalent cations (Al3+, Mg2+, Ca2+, Fe2+) chelate fluoroquinolones in the GI tract, preventing absorption.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Achilles Tendonitis in an Athlete
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 52-year-old recreational marathon runner treated for complicated UTI with ciprofloxacin.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: On day 6, develops intense pain and swelling over posterior heel while running.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What is the immediate pharmacological action?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Immediately discontinue ciprofloxacin, avoid weight-bearing exercise, and substitute with a non-quinolone antibiotic to prevent complete rupture of the Achilles tendon.

generics.name: Doxycycline
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Tetracycline Class Antibiotic (30S Ribosomal Subunit Inhibitor)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Broad-spectrum bacteriostatic antibiotic that reversibly binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit of susceptible bacteria. This prevents the access and binding of aminoacyl-tRNA to the ribosomal acceptor (A) site on the mRNA-ribosome complex, halting the elongation step of protein synthesis. Doxycycline has high lipid solubility, allowing excellent penetration into tissues, prostate, and bronchial secretions, and is safely eliminated via non-renal (biliary and fecal chelation) pathways.

indications.name: Rickettsial Infections (Scrub Typhus & Murine Typhus in Bangladesh)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: Drug of choice (DGHS Protocol)

indications.name: Severe Cholera (Vibrio cholerae) Epidemic Control
indications.note: Single 300 mg dose reduces duration and stool volume

indications.name: Chlamydial Urethritis, Cervicitis, and Pelvic Inflammatory Disease
Malaria Chemoprophylaxis (Chloroquine-resistant Plasmodium falciparum)
Acne Vulgaris and Rosacea (Anti-inflammatory & antimicrobial)

contraindications.reason: Chelates with calcium in developing fetal bones and teeth, causing permanent yellow-gray-brown discoloration and enamel hypoplasia

Cross-allergenicity

dosageGuidance.adult: Standard: 100 mg twice daily on day 1, then 100 mg once or twice daily for 7-14 days. Cholera: Single dose 300 mg. Malaria prophylaxis: 100 mg once daily starting 1-2 days before travel.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: Children > 8 years (> 45 kg): Adult dose. Under 45 kg: 2.2-4.4 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Standard adult dosing is safe.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take with a full glass of water while sitting or standing upright. Do NOT lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking to prevent pill-induced esophagitis and esophageal ulceration.

doseAdjustment.renal: No dose adjustment required in renal impairment (unlike other tetracyclines, it is eliminated via inactive fecal chelation). Safe in CKD.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Caution in severe hepatic impairment.

common: Gastrointestinal upset, nausea, vomiting, epigastric distress
rare: Benign intracranial hypertension (Pseudotumor cerebri — headache, papilledema)
seriousWarnings: Pill-Induced Esophageal Ulceration: Taking doxycycline dry or lying down immediately after ingestion can cause the capsule to lodge in the esophagus, causing chemical necrosis and deep esophageal ulcers. Always take with a full glass of water and remain upright for 30 minutes.

precautions: Avoid intense sunlight and tanning beds due to photosensitivity. Space out antacids, calcium, iron, and dairy products by at least 2 hours.

monitoringRequirements.parameter: Signs of Esophagitis (Retrosternal chest pain, odynophagia)
monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Discontinue and evaluate with endoscopy if severe

generics.foodInteractions: Dairy products, calcium, iron, and multivalent antacids decrease absorption through chelation. Take 2 hours apart.

pregnancyInfo.details: Causes permanent tooth discoloration and impaired bone growth in fetuses.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in breast milk; avoid during lactation to prevent infant tooth staining.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Contraindicated under 8 years of age (short course permissible in life-threatening rickettsial scrub typhus per AAP/CDC).
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Safe in elderly; non-renal elimination makes it advantageous in CKD.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, acute dizziness.
overdoseInformation.management: Supportive care; not dialyzable.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C in airtight containers protected from light. Outdated/degraded tetracyclines can cause Fanconi syndrome (nephrotoxicity).

bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: গর্ভবতী নারী এবং ৮ বছরের কম বয়সী শিশুদের ক্ষেত্রে দাঁতের স্থায়ী বিবর্ণতা এবং অস্থির বৃদ্ধি বাধার কারণে ব্যবহার নিষেধ।

vivaQuestions.question: Why is doxycycline safer than tetracycline in patients with renal failure?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: রেনাল ফেইলিওরে টেট্রাসাইক্লিনের চেয়ে ডক্সিসাইক্লিন নিরাপদ কেন?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Doxycycline is eliminated primarily via non-renal routes (biliary excretion and direct chelation in intestinal lumen), so it does not accumulate in kidney failure.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Does not require dosage adjustment in renal impairment.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is doxycycline contraindicated in pregnancy and young children under 8 years?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: গর্ভাবস্থায় এবং ৮ বছরের কম বয়সী শিশুদের ডক্সিসাইক্লিন নিষেধ কেন?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Doxycycline chelates with calcium orthophosphate in developing teeth and bones, causing permanent brownish discoloration and enamel hypoplasia.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Calcium chelation leads to permanent tooth staining.

recallFlashcards.front: Ribosomal target of Doxycycline?
recallFlashcards.back: 30S ribosomal subunit (A-site block).

recallFlashcards.front: Patient counseling to prevent esophageal ulceration?
recallFlashcards.back: Take with a full glass of water and remain upright for 30 minutes.

practiceSba.question: Drug of choice for Scrub Typhus (Orientia tsutsugamushi) and Cholera in Bangladesh is?
practiceSba.explanation: Doxycycline is the first-line antimicrobial for rickettsial infections, scrub typhus, and severe cholera.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Scrub Typhus with Eschar in North Bengal
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 38-year-old agricultural worker from Rangpur with high remittent fever, headache, and black necrotic eschar in groin.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Diagnosed with scrub typhus. Prescribed Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What is the expected therapeutic response time?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Rapid defervescence typically occurs within 24 to 48 hours of starting doxycycline in scrub typhus. Failure to respond suggests an alternate diagnosis.

generics.name: Metformin
generics.mechanismOfAction: First-line oral antihyperglycemic agent that increases AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) activity in hepatocytes and skeletal muscle. This suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis and glycogenolysis (reducing basal hepatic glucose output) and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity and glucose uptake via GLUT4 translocation. It does not stimulate pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion, meaning it does NOT cause hypoglycemia when used as monotherapy, and promotes mild weight loss or weight neutrality. It also delays intestinal glucose absorption.
generics.receptorOrTarget: AMP-Activated Protein Kinase (AMPK) & Mitochondrial Complex I

Symptoms include malaise, myalgia, respiratory distress, and abdominal pain. Discontinue immediately if metabolic acidosis is suspected.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Baseline and at least annually (every 3-6 months if eGFR 30-60)
monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Dose adjust or stop if eGFR < 30 mL/min

generics.foodInteractions: Taking with meals reduces abdominal cramps and diarrhea.

pregnancyInfo.details: Used extensively for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) when insulin is unavailable or refused; passes placenta without evident teratogenicity.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in small amounts in breast milk; safe during lactation.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Approved for children >= 10 years with T2DM.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Rigorously check eGFR; high risk of asymptomatic renal decline.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Profound lactic acidosis, hypothermia, hypotension, somnolence, coma (hypoglycemia does not typically occur unless combined with sulfonylureas).
overdoseInformation.management: Immediate hemodialysis to remove metformin and correct acid-base balance; sodium bicarbonate for severe acidosis.

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Metformin not cause hypoglycemia when used as monotherapy?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: মেটফর্মিন একা ব্যবহার করলে কেন রক্তের সুগার মারাত্মকভাবে নেমে (হাইপোগ্লাইসেমিয়া) যায় না?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Metformin is an insulin sensitizer (euglycemic agent) that reduces excessive hepatic glucose output and increases glucose uptake without stimulating pancreatic beta-cell insulin secretion.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Does not cause hypoglycemia and does not cause weight gain.

recallFlashcards.front: Molecular mechanism of Metformin?
recallFlashcards.back: Activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and inhibits mitochondrial complex I.

recallFlashcards.front: Cutoff eGFR for Metformin discontinuation?
recallFlashcards.back: Discontinue if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73m² due to lactic acidosis risk.

practiceSba.question: First-line pharmacological agent for overweight patients with newly diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (normal renal function)?
practiceSba.explanation: Metformin is the universally recommended first-line therapy (ADA, EASD, DGHS) with cardiovascular safety and weight-neutral/weight-loss profile.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Metformin-Associated Lactic Acidosis (MALA)
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 67-year-old male with T2DM on metformin 1000 mg BD develops acute dehydration and prerenal AKI from viral gastroenteritis.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Severe hyperventilation (Kussmaul breathing), deep lethargy, arterial pH 7.15, lactate 9.5 mmol/L, serum creatinine 4.2 mg/dL.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: Identify the condition and management.
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Metformin-associated lactic acidosis (MALA) triggered by acute renal failure accumulating metformin. Metformin must be stopped immediately; hemodialysis clears both lactate and metformin efficiently.

generics.name: Insulin (Regular / Soluble Human Insulin)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Identical to endogenous human pancreatic insulin produced by recombinant DNA technology. Binds to the extracellular alpha subunits of the heterotetrameric insulin receptor tyrosine kinase on cell surfaces (skeletal muscle, adipocytes, hepatocytes). This triggers autophosphorylation of intracellular beta subunits and activates insulin receptor substrates (IRS-1, IRS-2) and the PI3K-Akt signaling cascade. This induces rapid translocation of glucose transporter 4 (GLUT4) storage vesicles to the plasma membrane, driving glucose uptake into muscle and fat. It accelerates glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein synthesis while halting gluconeogenesis, glycogenolysis, lipolysis, and ketogenesis.

indications.name: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) and Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State (HHS) (Drug of Choice)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: Intravenous continuous infusion (0.1 units/kg/hour) per national DKA protocol

indications.name: Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus (Basal-bolus prandial glycemic control)
Type 2 Diabetes during Acute Illness, Sepsis, Surgery, and Pregnancy (GDM)
Severe Acute Hyperkalemia (Shift K+ into cells with 25-50% Dextrose)

contraindications.reason: Can precipitate fatal neuroglycopenic coma and irreversible brain damage

contraindications.condition: Known hypersensitivity to human insulin or formulation excipients
contraindications.reason: Rare anaphylaxis

dosageGuidance.adult: Subcutaneous: 0.2 to 1.0 unit/kg/day total insulin, with regular insulin providing 50% as prandial doses divided 30 minutes before main meals. DKA Protocol: IV regular insulin bolus 0.1 unit/kg, followed by continuous infusion of 0.1 unit/kg/hour; titrate to lower glucose by 50-75 mg/dL/hour.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: Individualized by pediatric endocrinologist based on carbohydrate counting.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Higher target HbA1c (7.5-8.0%) to prevent hypoglycemia falls.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Subcutaneous injection must be given 30 minutes before meals. Regular insulin is the ONLY insulin formulation that can be administered intravenously.

doseAdjustment.renal: Insulin clearance is prolonged in renal impairment; dose reduction required in CKD to prevent severe hypoglycemia.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Impaired hepatic gluconeogenesis and clearance require careful blood glucose titration.

common: Lipohypertrophy (fat deposits at unrotated injection sites)
uncommon: Transient visual blurriness upon starting (osmotic lens changes)
seriousWarnings: Emergency: Severe Hypoglycemia. Blood glucose < 3.0 mmol/L can cause irreversible brain injury and death within hours. Ensure patient and family are trained to recognize warning signs and administer oral sugar or IV 25% dextrose.

precautions: Rotate injection sites (abdomen, thigh, upper arm) with each dose to prevent lipodystrophy. Never give regular insulin IV without checking potassium in DKA.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Pre-meal and bedtime (at least 4 times daily in intensive regimens)

monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Add KCl to IV fluids once K+ < 5.0 mmol/L to prevent fatal hypokalemia

generics.foodInteractions: Inject 30 minutes before meal. Skipping meals after injection causes severe hypoglycemia.

pregnancyInfo.category: Category B / Gold Standard in Pregnancy
pregnancyInfo.details: Does not cross the placenta; gold standard treatment for Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) and pre-existing diabetes.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Endogenous protein destroyed in infant digestive tract; completely safe during lactation.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Mandatory lifelong therapy in Type 1 diabetes. Careful monitoring during growth spurts.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: High risk of hypoglycemia unawareness. Less stringent glycemic targets recommended.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Neuroglycopenia: Palpitations, diaphoresis, hunger, confusion, seizures, coma, death.
overdoseInformation.management: Conscious patient: 15-20 g fast-acting oral carbohydrates (fruit juice, sugar water). Unconscious patient: 25-50 ml of 25% Dextrose IV bolus or 1 mg Glucagon IM/SC.

generics.storageInformation: Unopened vials must be stored in refrigerator at 2°C to 8°C (Do NOT freeze). In-use vial can be kept at room temperature (below 30°C) away from direct sunlight for up to 28 days.

bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: খাবারের ৩০ মিনিট পূর্বে ত্বকের নিচে (সাবকিউটেনিয়াস) ইনজেকশন নিন। ইনজেকশনের স্থান পরিবর্তন (রোটেশন) করুন।
bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: মারাত্মক হাইপোগ্লাইসেমিয়া (ঘাম, কাঁপুনি, বিভ্রান্তি) দেখা দিলে তাৎক্ষণিক চিনি বা মিষ্টি শরবত পান করুন।

vivaQuestions.question: Why is Regular Insulin the only insulin suitable for intravenous administration in Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA)?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: ডায়াবেটিক কিটোঅ্যাসিডোসিসে (DKA) কেবল রেগুলার ইনসুলিনই শিরাপথে (IV) কেন দেওয়া যায়?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Regular insulin is a clear, soluble hexamer in zinc solution that dissociates rapidly into active monomers in systemic circulation without delayed precipitate formation or protamine additives.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Neutral regular insulin is the only form approved for continuous IV infusion in DKA.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the molecular mechanism of insulin-induced hypokalemia?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: ইনসুলিন রক্তে পটাশিয়াম কমায় কীভাবে?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Insulin directly stimulates the Na+/K+-ATPase pump in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue, pumping potassium into cells and lowering serum potassium.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Used therapeutically in emergency hyperkalemia along with dextrose.

recallFlashcards.front: Transporter stimulated by insulin in muscle and adipose tissue?
recallFlashcards.back: GLUT4 (glucose transporter type 4).

recallFlashcards.front: Onset and peak of regular subcutaneous insulin?
recallFlashcards.back: Onset: 30 minutes; Peak: 2-3 hours; Duration: 6-8 hours.

practiceSba.question: In the emergency management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA), which insulin regimen is universally indicated?
options: Continuous low-dose IV Regular Insulin (0.1 U/kg/h)
practiceSba.explanation: Continuous low-dose IV infusion of regular insulin provides predictable clearance, halts lipolysis, and suppresses hepatic gluconeogenesis.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) in Newly Diagnosed Type 1 Diabetes
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 17-year-old girl presents with deep sighing Kussmaul breathing, fruity acetone breath, blood glucose 28 mmol/L, ketonuria 4+, and arterial pH 7.10.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Initiated on fluid resuscitation with normal saline and IV regular insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hour.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: When should potassium replacement be initiated during insulin infusion?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Insulin shifts potassium into cells; if serum K+ is < 5.0 mmol/L, potassium replacement (20-30 mmol/L IV fluid) must be added immediately to prevent fatal hypokalemic cardiac arrest.

generics.name: Salbutamol (Albuterol)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Selective agonist of beta-2 adrenergic receptors located predominantly on bronchial smooth muscle. Gs-protein activation stimulates adenylyl cyclase, converting ATP into intracellular cyclic AMP (cAMP). Elevated cAMP activates protein kinase A (PKA), which inhibits myosin light chain kinase and lowers intracellular calcium concentrations. This produces rapid, potent relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle, reversing acute bronchoconstriction within 5 minutes. It also inhibits mediator release from mast cells and increases mucociliary clearance.

indications.name: Acute Bronchospasm in Bronchial Asthma (Reliever Therapy)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: First-line reliever for acute asthma exacerbation (GINA & DGHS Guidelines)

indications.name: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) Exacerbation
Exercise-Induced Bronchoconstriction Prevention
Adjunctive Therapy for Severe Hyperkalemia (Nebulization)
indications.note: Shifts K+ into cells via Na+/K+ ATPase stimulation

contraindications.reason: Anaphylaxis
Not indicated for tocolysis in early pregnancy

dosageGuidance.adult: MDI Inhaler: 100 to 200 mcg (1-2 puffs) as needed for acute relief (Max 800 mcg/day). Nebulization: 2.5 mg to 5 mg nebulized with oxygen over 10-15 minutes every 20-30 minutes for acute severe asthma. Oral: 2-4 mg three to four times daily (less preferred due to systemic side effects).
dosageGuidance.paediatric: MDI with spacer: 100-200 mcg (1-2 puffs). Nebulizer: 2.5 mg.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Initial lower dose (2 mg oral); monitor pulse for tachycardia.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Inhaled route is vastly superior to oral tablets due to immediate bronchodilation and minimal systemic tremor/tachycardia.

doseAdjustment.renal: No dose adjustment required.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: No dose adjustment required.

common: Fine skeletal muscle tremors (especially hands, mediated by peripheral beta-2 receptors)
seriousWarnings: Over-Reliance Warning: Heavy reliance on SABA inhalers (> 1 canister/month) without inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) is a major risk factor for fatal asthma attacks due to beta-receptor down-regulation and unaddressed airway inflammation.

precautions: Use with spacer chamber in children and elderly to maximize lung deposition. Caution in severe hyperthyroidism and tachyarrhythmias.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Before and 15-30 min after nebulization in acute asthma
In frequent nebulization or IV therapy

generics.foodInteractions: Inhaled route bypasses gastrointestinal absorption.

pregnancyInfo.category: Category C / Preferred SABA in Pregnancy
pregnancyInfo.details: Extensive safety record; first-line bronchodilator of choice during pregnancy (GINA).

breastfeedingInfo.details: Small amounts in breast milk; compatible with breastfeeding.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Metered dose inhaler with a dedicated spacer device (with or without mask) is the gold standard.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Caution in elderly with ischemic heart disease or arrhythmias due to tachycardia.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Pronounced skeletal muscle tremor, extreme tachycardia, palpitations, chest pain, hypokalemia, metabolic acidosis.
overdoseInformation.management: Discontinue drug. Cardioselective beta-1 blocker (e.g. Metoprolol/Bisoprolol) can cautiously reverse cardiovascular toxicity in non-asthmatics.

generics.storageInformation: Store inhalers below 30°C. Protect from direct frost and heat. Do not puncture or burn pressurized canister.

vivaQuestions.question: Why does Salbutamol produce hand tremors as a common side effect?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: সালবিউটামল সেবনে হাত কাঁপে (ট্রে মর) কেন?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Skeletal muscle twitch and tremor is mediated by stimulation of beta-2 adrenergic receptors in skeletal muscle fibers, altering twitch kinetics and tension development.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Tremor is the most common dose-limiting adverse effect.

recallFlashcards.front: Cellular mechanism of Salbutamol bronchodilation?
recallFlashcards.back: Increases intracellular cAMP -> lowers intracellular calcium in bronchial smooth muscle.

recallFlashcards.front: Electrolyte disturbance caused by high-dose Salbutamol?
recallFlashcards.back: Hypokalemia (stimulates Na+/K+ ATPase, driving K+ into cells).

practiceSba.question: First-line inhaled rescue bronchodilator for acute bronchial asthma attack is?
practiceSba.explanation: Salbutamol is a rapid-acting selective beta-2 agonist producing bronchodilation within 5 minutes.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Acute Severe Asthma & Excessive Beta-Agonist Use
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 22-year-old female medical student presents with acute dyspnea, unable to complete sentences in one breath, PEFR 40% predicted.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Has used 18 puffs of salbutamol over 2 hours without relief; pulse 135 bpm, fine hand tremor.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What is the immediate emergency pharmacological management?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Administer oxygen, back-to-back nebulized Salbutamol (5 mg) plus Ipratropium (0.5 mg), and immediate systemic corticosteroids (IV Hydrocortisone or oral Prednisolone) to upregulate down-regulated beta receptors.

generics.name: Dexamethasone
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Long-Acting Glucocorticoid (High Potency, Zero Mineralocorticoid Activity)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Synthetic glucocorticoid with 25 to 30 times higher anti-inflammatory potency than hydrocortisone and virtually zero mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) activity. Binds to intracellular glucocorticoid receptors (GR), translocating into the nucleus to activate anti-inflammatory genes (transactivation of IκB-alpha, lipocortin-1/annexin-1) and inhibit pro-inflammatory transcription factors (transrepression of NF-κB and AP-1). This profoundly suppresses synthesis of phospholipase A2, COX-2, inducible nitric oxide synthase, and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-2, IL-6, TNF-alpha).

indications.name: Cerebral Edema (Associated with Brain Tumors, Craniotomy, or Meningitis)

indications.name: Bacterial Meningitis Adjunct (Given with or before first antibiotic dose)

contraindications.reason: Risk of disseminated vaccine-strain infection

dosageGuidance.geriatric: Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration; monitor blood glucose.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take oral doses in the morning with food to mimic diurnal cortisol rhythm and minimize insomnia.

doseAdjustment.renal: No dose adjustment required.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Dose reduction and close monitoring in severe chronic liver disease.

rare: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head

precautions: Always monitor blood glucose in diabetics. Never stop prolonged courses abruptly. In Dengue fever, steroids are NOT recommended and may exacerbate bleeding (DGHS 2024).

Steroids mask fever and signs of peritonitis/sepsis

pregnancyInfo.details: Crosses placenta; indicated specifically for antenatal acceleration of fetal lung maturity in threatened preterm birth.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in low levels; short courses are compatible with breastfeeding.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Highly effective in croup and meningitis. Avoid chronic prolonged use to prevent growth stunting.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: High risk of acute confusion, delirium, severe hyperglycemia, and rapid osteoporosis.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Extreme agitation, acute psychosis, severe hyperglycemia, gastrointestinal bleeding.
overdoseInformation.management: Symptomatic supportive therapy; gradual dose taper. Hemodialysis is not effective.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C protected from light.

bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: সকালে খাবারের সাথে সেবন করুন যাতে ঘুমের ব্যাঘাত না ঘটে। চিকিৎসকের পরামর্শ ব্যতীত হঠাৎ খাওয়া বন্ধ করবেন না।

pharmacologyLearning.pathwaySummary: Binds glucocorticoid receptor -> transactivation of Annexin-A1 (inhibits PLA2) + transrepression of NF-kB -> suppresses inflammatory cytokines.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is Dexamethasone preferred over Hydrocortisone in cerebral edema?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: মস্তিষ্কের ইডিমা বা ফোলায় হাইড্রোকর্টিসনের চেয়ে ডেক্সামিথাসন কেন পছন্দনীয়?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Dexamethasone has 25-30 times the anti-inflammatory potency of hydrocortisone with zero mineralocorticoid (sodium/fluid retaining) activity, avoiding any increase in intracranial volume.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Zero mineralocorticoid potency makes it drug of choice for vasogenic cerebral edema.

recallFlashcards.front: Mineralocorticoid potency of Dexamethasone?
recallFlashcards.back: Zero (virtually no salt or water retention).

recallFlashcards.front: Why must prolonged steroid courses be tapered gradually?
recallFlashcards.back: To allow atrophied adrenal cortex time to recover endogenous cortisol synthesis and prevent acute adrenal crisis.

practiceSba.question: Which corticosteroid is administered antenatally to a pregnant mother in threatened preterm labor at 30 weeks to accelerate fetal lung maturation?
practiceSba.explanation: Dexamethasone and Betamethasone cross the placenta in active form and stimulate surfactant synthesis by fetal type II alveolar pneumocytes.

clinicalCaseScenario.title: Acute Croup (Laryngotracheobronchitis) in a Toddler
clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 2-year-old child presents with barking seal-like cough, inspiratory stridor, and hoarseness.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Single dose of oral dexamethasone (0.15 mg/kg) is administered.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: What is the clinical benefit and timeframe of dexamethasone in croup?
clinicalCaseScenario.discussion: Oral dexamethasone reduces laryngeal mucosal edema within 1-2 hours, decreasing hospital admissions, need for nebulized epinephrine, and intubation.

generics.name: Paracetamol + Caffeine
generics.pharmacologicalClass: Fixed-Dose Combination Analgesic (Central Analgesic + CNS Stimulant / Adenosine Antagonist)
generics.mechanismOfAction: Combines the central cyclooxygenase-inhibiting antipyretic and analgesic action of paracetamol (500 mg) with the central adenosine receptor (A1 and A2A) antagonism of caffeine (65 mg). Caffeine constricts dilated cerebral blood vessels (providing specific relief in vascular tension and migraine headaches) and acts as an analgesic adjuvant, accelerating paracetamol absorption and enhancing pain-relieving potency by approximately 40% compared to paracetamol alone.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Central Cyclooxygenase & Central Adenosine A1/A2A Receptors

indications.name: Tension Headache, Migraine Attack, and Severe Body Aches
Acute Dental Pain and Post-extraction Discomfort
Primary Dysmenorrhea and Musculoskeletal Aches

contraindications.reason: High risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity
Caffeine stimulates tachycardia and palpitations

dosageGuidance.adult: 1 to 2 tablets every 4 to 6 hours as needed (Maximum 8 tablets = 4000 mg Paracetamol + 520 mg Caffeine in 24 hours).
dosageGuidance.paediatric: Not recommended for children under 12 years of age.
dosageGuidance.geriatric: Adult dosing acceptable; monitor for caffeine-induced insomnia and palpitations.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take with a glass of water. Avoid taking late at night if prone to insomnia.

doseAdjustment.renal: Space doses to every 6-8 hours in eGFR < 30 mL/min.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Reduce dose in chronic liver disease; avoid in decompensated cirrhosis.

uncommon: Tachycardia, mild elevation of blood pressure
seriousWarnings: Paracetamol Toxicity Warning: Never combine with other paracetamol-containing cold/fever medications. Total 24h paracetamol must not exceed 4000 mg.

precautions: Limit concurrent consumption of caffeine-containing beverages (coffee, tea, energy drinks). Do not use in Dengue fever (pure paracetamol preferred).
generics.foodInteractions: May be taken with or without food.

pregnancyInfo.details: High caffeine intake in pregnancy is associated with low birth weight. Pure paracetamol is preferred during pregnancy.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Caffeine passes into breast milk and can cause irritability and insomnia in the infant.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Contraindicated under 12 years of age.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Higher sensitivity to caffeine-induced tachycardia, tremors, and sleep disturbance.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Paracetamol hepatotoxicity combined with caffeine toxicity (arrhythmias, seizures, severe vomiting).
overdoseInformation.management: Immediate IV N-Acetylcysteine (NAC) for paracetamol toxicity. Supportive beta-blockers for severe caffeine-induced supraventricular tachycardias.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 25°C in a dry place.

vivaQuestions.question: What is the pharmacological rationale for adding Caffeine to Paracetamol in tension headaches?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: টেনশন হেডেকের ক্ষেত্রে প্যারাসিটামলের সাথে ক্যাফেইন যোগ করার ফার্মাকোলজিক্যাল যুক্তি কী?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Caffeine blocks adenosine receptors causing cranial vasoconstriction, stimulates gastric emptying to accelerate paracetamol absorption, and directly enhances analgesic efficacy by approximately 40%.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Analgesic adjuvant action without requiring higher opioid doses.

recallFlashcards.front: Role of caffeine in paracetamol combinations?

practiceSba.question: Caffeine enhances the analgesic efficacy of paracetamol primarily by acting as an antagonist at which receptor?

generics.name: Paracetamol
generics.mechanismOfAction: Paracetamol exerts analgesic and antipyretic effects primarily through central inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis by cyclooxygenase (COX-1, COX-2, and putative central splice variant), with negligible peripheral anti-inflammatory action due to high cellular peroxide levels in inflamed tissues. It lowers body temperature by acting on the hypothalamic thermoregulatory center to stimulate peripheral vasodilation and sweating. AM404, an active hepatic/brain metabolite, also stimulates cannabinoid CB1 receptors and TRPV1 channels to inhibit nociceptive transmission.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Central Cyclooxygenase & Cannabinoid CB1 / TRPV1 Receptors via AM404 metabolite

indications.name: Pyrexia / Fever (First-line antipyretic in viral illness and Dengue)
indications.guidelineRecommendation: Strict drug of choice in Dengue Fever (DGHS National Dengue Guideline 2024; NSAIDs strictly contraindicated)

indications.name: Mild to Moderate Acute Pain (Headache, toothache, dysmenorrhea, post-vaccination)
Osteoarthritis (Symptomatic first-line mild pain relief)

contraindications.condition: Severe acute hepatic failure or active severe liver disease
contraindications.reason: High risk of irreversible fatal centrilobular hepatic necrosis
Anaphylactoid or severe cutaneous adverse reactions

dosageGuidance.adult: 500 mg - 1000 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum: 4000 mg (4.0 g) in 24 hours.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: 10 to 15 mg/kg per dose orally every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Maximum: 60 mg/kg per 24 hours.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: May be taken with or without food. When rapid analgesic onset is needed, taking on an empty stomach with a full glass of water accelerates gastric emptying.

doseAdjustment.renal: eGFR 10-50 mL/min: Increase dosing interval to every 6 hours. eGFR < 10 mL/min: Increase interval to every 8 hours.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Mild to moderate hepatic impairment: Maximum 2000 mg (2 g) per 24 hours. Severe cirrhosis: Contraindicated.

seriousWarnings: Hepatotoxicity: Doses exceeding 4g/24h or single ingestion > 7.5g cause acute hepatic necrosis and liver failure.
Dengue Warning: Never substitute or combine with Aspirin or NSAIDs in febrile patients due to fatal bleeding risk.
Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome, Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis) reported rarely.

precautions: Chronic malnutrition, anorexia, or severe dehydration reduces glutathione reserves and lowers the toxic threshold.
Chronic alcoholism induces CYP2E1, accelerating toxic NAPQI formation.
Always warn patients to check labels of OTC cough/cold preparations to avoid accidental cumulative overdose.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Baseline in chronic use; immediate serial levels in suspected overdose
monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Elevation > 3x ULN warrants dose reduction; > 1000 U/L indicates severe necrosis.
INR > 2.0 indicates acute liver failure requiring intensive care and NAC.
Rising creatinine indicates hepatorenal syndrome or acute tubular necrosis.

generics.foodInteractions: May be taken with food to reduce minor gastric upset, though food may slightly delay peak absorption. High-pectin meals can delay absorption.

pregnancyInfo.details: Analgesic and antipyretic of choice in all trimesters of pregnancy when clinically indicated, at lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in human milk in small amounts; maternal therapeutic doses are safe and compatible with breastfeeding (AAP & WHO).

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Weight-based dosing (10-15 mg/kg every 4-6 hours) must be strictly calculated; avoid teaspoon estimation. Paracetamol drops and syrups must use provided calibrated oral syringes.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: Use standard starting doses, but evaluate chronic nutritional state and alcohol intake. Frail elderly patients with reduced hepatic glutathione may have lower toxicity threshold.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Phase 1 (0-24h): Nausea, vomiting, pallor; Phase 2 (24-48h): Right upper quadrant pain, elevated ALT/AST; Phase 3 (72-96h): Jaundice, encephalopathy, coagulopathy, hypoglycemia, renal failure.
overdoseInformation.management: Check serum paracetamol level on Rumack-Matthew nomogram 4 hours post-ingestion. Administer activated charcoal if presentation is within 1-2 hours.
overdoseInformation.antidote: Intravenous or oral N-acetylcysteine (NAC). Most effective when initiated within 8 hours of ingestion to replenish hepatic glutathione and conjugate toxic NAPQI.

generics.storageInformation: Store below 30°C in a dry place protected from direct heat, moisture, and light. Keep in original blister packaging.

bilingualNotes.mechanismSummaryBn: মস্তিষ্কের হাইপোথ্যালামাসে প্রোস্টাগ্ল্যান্ডিন সংশ্লেষণ কমিয়ে জ্বর দ্রুত কমায় এবং কেন্দ্রীয় ব্যথার পথকে নিয়ন্ত্রণ করে মাঝারি ব্যথা দূর করে। পেরিফেরাল প্রদাহে কাজ করে না। ডেঙ্গু জ্বরে এটি একমাত্র নির্দেশিত ও নিরাপদ ব্যথানাশক।
bilingualNotes.patientCounsellingBn: দিনে সর্বোচ্চ ৪ গ্রাম (৮টি ৫০০ মিগ্রা ট্যাবলেট) এর বেশি খাবেন না। অ্যালকোহল এড়িয়ে চলুন। অন্য যেকোনো ওষুধে প্যারাসিটামল আছে কি না যাচাই করুন। ডেঙ্গু জ্বরে ভুলেও অ্যাসপিরিন বা অন্য ব্যথানাশক খাবেন না।
bilingualNotes.criticalWarningBn: একবারে মাত্রাতিরিক্ত (১০-১৫টি ট্যাবলেট) সেবনে লিভারের কোষ ধ্বংস হয়ে মারাত্মক ও প্রাণঘাতী হেপাটিক ফেইলিউর হতে পারে। ডেঙ্গু জ্বরে কখনো অ্যাসপিরিন বা ডাইক্লোফেনাক খাবেন না, কেবল প্যারাসিটামল ব্যবহার করুন।

pharmacologyLearning.pathwaySummary: Rapid GI absorption -> CYP2E1 (5-10%) generates NAPQI -> conjugated by glutathione -> central COX inhibition + AM404 cannabinoid/TRPV1 activation -> antipyresis and analgesia.

vivaQuestions.question: Why is Paracetamol safe in Dengue Fever while Aspirin and Ibuprofen are strictly contraindicated?
vivaQuestions.questionBn: ডেঙ্গু জ্বরে অ্যাসপিরিন ও আইবুপ্রোফেন সম্পূর্ণ নিষিদ্ধ অথচ প্যারাসিটামল কেন নিরাপদ?
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: Dengue virus causes thrombocytopenia and capillary fragility. Aspirin irreversibly inhibits platelet COX-1 and thromboxane A2, while NSAIDs reversibly inhibit platelets and cause gastric mucosal erosions, triggering catastrophic gastrointestinal hemorrhage and dengue shock syndrome. Paracetamol acts centrally with negligible peripheral platelet COX-1 inhibition, preserving platelet function and hemostasis.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: Core national guideline requirement: Only paracetamol for dengue fever analgesia/antipyresis.

vivaQuestions.question: Explain the biochemical basis of Paracetamol toxicity and the mechanism of its antidote.
vivaQuestions.questionBn: প্যারাসিটামল বিষক্রিয়ার জৈব-রাসায়নিক কারণ এবং এর অ্যান্টিডোটের কার্যপদ্ধতি ব্যাখ্যা করুন।
vivaQuestions.modelAnswer: At therapeutic doses, ~90% of paracetamol is safely conjugated via glucuronidation and sulfation. ~5-10% is metabolized by CYP2E1 to NAPQI, which is neutralized by glutathione. In overdose, sulfation/glucuronidation saturate; excess NAPQI depletes hepatic glutathione and covalently binds to mitochondrial proteins, causing centrilobular hepatic necrosis. The antidote is N-acetylcysteine (NAC), which acts as a glutathione precursor and direct sulfhydryl donor to conjugate NAPQI.
vivaQuestions.highYieldPearl: NAC within 8 hours provides near-complete hepatoprotection.

recallFlashcards.front: Toxic metabolite of paracetamol responsible for hepatic necrosis?
recallFlashcards.back: NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine).

recallFlashcards.front: Specific antidote for paracetamol overdose?
recallFlashcards.back: N-acetylcysteine (NAC) - replenishes glutathione.

recallFlashcards.front: Maximum recommended adult daily dose of paracetamol?
recallFlashcards.back: 4000 mg (4.0 g) per 24 hours.

practiceSba.question: A 20-year-old male presents 6 hours after ingesting 15 grams of paracetamol in a suicide attempt. What is the immediate pharmacological intervention?
practiceSba.explanation: Intravenous N-acetylcysteine administered within 8 hours of paracetamol ingestion replenishes hepatic glutathione stores and prevents fatal centrilobular necrosis.

clinicalCaseScenario.patientProfile: 28-year-old male in Dhaka presents during dengue epidemic with 3-day history of high fever (103°F), retro-orbital headache, and severe arthralgia. Dengue NS1 Ag positive, platelets 90,000/uL.
clinicalCaseScenario.presentation: Patient asks if he can take Ketorolac or Diclofenac for the severe body pain. Doctor prescribes Paracetamol 500 mg TDS.
clinicalCaseScenario.clinicalQuestion: Why must NSAIDs be strictly avoided in this patient?

generics.name: Omeprazole
generics.mechanismOfAction: Omeprazole is a substituted benzimidazole prodrug that accumulates selectively in the acidic secretory canaliculi of parietal cells. Protonation converts it to active sulfenamide, which forms a covalent disulfide bond with Cys813 of the luminal H+/K+-ATPase pump. This irreversibly blocks the final common pathway of gastric acid secretion, inhibiting both basal and stimulated acid production regardless of the secretagogue.
generics.receptorOrTarget: Luminal Cys813 of H+/K+-ATPase Proton Pump on Gastric Parietal Cells

indications.name: Peptic Ulcer Disease (Duodenal & Gastric Ulcer Healing)
Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) & Erosive Esophagitis
Helicobacter pylori Eradication Triple Therapy
indications.guidelineRecommendation: Combined with Amoxicillin and Clarithromycin for 14 days

contraindications.reason: Anaphylaxis or acute interstitial nephritis

contraindications.condition: Concomitant use with Rilpivirine or Atazanavir
contraindications.reason: Loss of antiretroviral therapeutic efficacy due to elevated gastric pH

dosageGuidance.adult: 20 mg to 40 mg once daily before breakfast for 4 to 8 weeks.
dosageGuidance.paediatric: 1 mg/kg once daily for severe GERD.
dosageGuidance.timingNotice: Take 30 to 60 minutes before morning breakfast so peak plasma concentrations coincide with activation of proton pumps.

doseAdjustment.renal: No dose adjustment necessary in renal failure or dialysis.
doseAdjustment.hepatic: Severe cirrhosis: Maximum 20 mg once daily due to increased bioavailability and prolonged half-life.

seriousWarnings: Drug interaction with Clopidogrel: Strong CYP2C19 inhibition blunts clopidogrel bioactivation; switch to Pantoprazole in cardiac stent patients.
Clostridioides difficile colitis risk due to prolonged acid suppression.
Long-term risks: Hypomagnesemia, Vitamin B12 deficiency, and osteoporotic hip fractures.

precautions: Always rule out gastric malignancy before initiating long-term therapy because symptomatic relief can delay diagnosis.
Monitor serum magnesium prior to and periodically during long-term therapy.

monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Hypomagnesemia requires oral/IV magnesium and possible PPI discontinuation.

monitoringRequirements.frequency: Annual evaluation in prolonged therapy (> 2 years)
monitoringRequirements.targetOrClinicalAction: Low B12 warrants supplementation or parenteral replacement.

generics.foodInteractions: Food reduces rate and extent of absorption; must be administered on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before morning breakfast.

pregnancyInfo.details: Extensive epidemiological studies show no increased risk of congenital malformations; short courses acceptable when clinically required.

breastfeedingInfo.details: Excreted in low amounts in breast milk; degraded rapidly by infant gastric acid.

generics.paediatricConsiderations: Approved for severe GERD and erosive esophagitis in children >= 1 year (1 mg/kg once daily). Capsule contents can be opened and mixed in apple sauce if unable to swallow.
generics.geriatricConsiderations: No dosage reduction needed based solely on age; evaluate long-term risk of hip fractures and hypomagnesemia in elderly patients taking concomitant diuretics.

overdoseInformation.symptoms: Confusion, drowsiness, blurred vision, tachycardia, nausea, sweating.
overdoseInformation.management: No specific antidote; symptomatic and supportive care. Hemodialysis is not effective due to high protein binding (~95%).

generics.storageInformation: Store below 30°C in tight, light-resistant container. Keep capsules in desiccated container away from humid bathroom storage.
